evidence.why: Six literal words and three double loads establish the representation and consumption, not compiled alignment.

facts.rationale: Preserves the supported constant representation while removing the unsupported inference that lfd proves compiled alignment.
facts.value: The source declares a file-local constant array `static const unsigned long __constants[6]`. Its consecutive big-endian word pairs are consumed as binary64 values at offsets 0, 8, and 16: 0.0 (0x0000000000000000), 2^32 (0x41F0000000000000), and 2^31 (0x41E0000000000000). Source declaration and loads alone do not establish compiled section extent or 8-byte alignment.

evidence.why: Complete raw variable-shift sequence; no validation of the full requested count.

facts.rationale: Corrects the baseline's unqualified out-of-range-zero claim without changing the supported register ABI or normal shift behavior.
facts.value: Consumes high:low words in r3:r4 and count n in r5, returning the logical-right-shifted pair in r3:r4. For n=0 it preserves the pair. For n=1–31, low becomes (low >> n) | (high << (32-n)) and high becomes high >> n. For n=32–63, low becomes high >> (n-32) and high becomes zero. Derived counts 32-n and n-32 allow a branchless sequence. These formulas are restricted to 0–63: PowerPC variable word shifts use the low six count bits, so arbitrary counts outside the word range are not universally suppressed.
